title: The Painted Cipher
premise: True-crime podcaster Orsen Okonkwo has built a quiet career proving that 'accidents' were murders, and his latest obsession is the 1997 disappearance of Ada Nwosu, a young archivist whose diary was found in a flooded basement. When a second, continuing volume of the diary surfaces—written in her hand years after she vanished—Orsen realizes Ada faked her death to escape the men she'd witnessed committing a crime, and that someone is now killing anyone who gets close to the truth. As he follows the diary's coded references to paintings hidden across the city, Orsen must decide whether exposing Ada will save her or destroy the invisible life she paid everything to build. In the end, he finds her alive, chooses justice over fame by airing the killers' confession instead of her location, and helps her step out of hiding on her own terms.
about_author: Mirabel Okafor is a former forensic archivist who left government work to write fiction after discovering how many case files end in convenient silence. She lives between Lagos and Lisbon, where she collects orphaned photographs and insists every story she tells began with a document someone wanted burned.

chapters.title: Three Accidents
chapters.summary: Orsen Okonkwo, in his own POV, records the finale of his podcast season, recapping the three deaths he proved were murders. The emotional beat is quiet triumph undercut by loneliness—his wins have cost him friends and made him paranoid. A listener's email arrives: someone claims to have the missing diary of Ada Nwosu, the case that started it all.

chapters.title: The Basement Volume
chapters.summary: Orsen meets the anonymous seller in a rain-soaked parking garage and buys the water-stained diary. Reading it that night, he finds entries that stop on the date Ada vanished. The beat is dread: the seller's parting words—'there's a second book'—hang over him as he notices someone watching his building.

chapters.title: Entries After the End
chapters.summary: A second package arrives: a continuation diary, dated years after Ada's disappearance, in handwriting Orsen verifies against archival records. Everyone swears Ada is dead; her mother wept at a closed casket. The beat is vertigo—either a brilliant forgery or a living witness everyone buried. Orsen begins decoding the diary's references to paintings.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Hand
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter from Ada Nwosu's POV, 1997: a meticulous young archivist discovers altered evidence logs implicating a respected police commander. Her fear builds as she copies documents and hides originals inside framed paintings at a restoration studio. The beat is the birth of a plan to disappear.

chapters.title: What the Frame Remembers
chapters.summary: Orsen tracks the diary's first cipher to a deconsecrated chapel where one of the paintings still hangs. Behind the canvas: a microfilm sleeve and a warning note in Ada's hand—'the third accident was a rehearsal.' The beat is exhilaration curdling into fear as he realizes the killer is following the same trail.

chapters.title: Commander Eze's Quiet Years
chapters.summary: Orsen profiles retired Commander Daniel Eze, now a philanthropist with a foundation named for his late wife. Interviews with former colleagues reveal a pattern: witnesses who died in accidents, all signed off by the same coroner. The beat is cold fury at how respectability launders violence.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Wept Twice
chapters.summary: Orsen visits Ada's mother, Grace, whose grief seems rehearsed in places and raw in others. She slips: 'She wrote to me after.' Orsen realizes Grace has known for years. The beat is moral complication—the mother chose her daughter's survival over the truth, and asks him to stop digging.

chapters.title: Restorer's Daughter
chapters.summary: From Ada's POV, 1998, one year into hiding: working under a new name in a coastal town, she learns the restoration trade and watches news of the 'accidents' that erase her old life's witnesses. The beat is survivor's guilt—every death buys her another year, and she keeps a ledger of the price.

chapters.title: A Podcast Gets Loud
chapters.summary: Orsen releases a teaser episode about the continuing diary; downloads explode and so do threats. His producer, Tunde, begs him to delay. That night his apartment is searched, professionally, nothing taken. The beat is the cost of visibility—Orsen, the man who exposes hidden lives, realizes he can no longer have one.

chapters.title: The Coroner's Confession
chapters.summary: Orsen finds the retired coroner, now dying, who admits he falsified reports for Eze but claims the last signature—on Ada's death certificate—was forged before the body arrived. The beat is a hinge: the death was staged by someone inside Eze's circle, meaning Ada had a protector with access.

chapters.title: Inside the Foundation
chapters.summary: Orsen infiltrates an Eze Foundation gala using a press credential. He photographs a private gallery of restored paintings—and recognizes the studio's watermark from the diary. Eze himself greets him, courteous and knowing, and mentions Orsen's podcast by name. The beat is the predator showing its teeth politely.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Prices
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, present day: she has been watching Orsen's investigation from a distance, torn between gratitude and terror. When she learns Eze's people have identified her mother as their path to her, she breaks her own rules and makes contact—leaving a cipher message for Orsen in a gallery listing. The beat is the invisible choosing to move.

chapters.title: Two Ciphers, One Hand
chapters.summary: Orsen decodes Ada's message and they meet in a night market, her face half-hidden. She gives him terms: find the final painting's proof, but never say her name aloud. He agrees, then discovers a tracker in his bag—he led Eze's fixer, a man called Silas, straight to the market. The beat is betrayal by his own carelessness.

chapters.title: Grace's Door
chapters.summary: Silas visits Grace Nwosu, and Orsen, tipped by Ada, arrives too late to stop the intimidation but in time to record it. Grace, defiant, burns a decade of letters rather than surrender them. The beat is fierce maternal courage—and the realization that Eze now knows Ada is alive.

chapters.title: The Last Painting
chapters.summary: The diary's final cipher points to a painting donated anonymously to a regional museum: inside its frame, the original 1997 evidence logs and a recording Ada made of Eze ordering a murder. But the museum's records show the painting was 'borrowed' three days ago. The beat is the trap snapping shut—Eze has the proof.

chapters.title: What Silas Keeps
chapters.summary: Ada's POV: she intercepts Silas, who reveals a fracture in Eze's circle—Silas has kept insurance files of his own for years, waiting for leverage. Ada offers him the one thing Eze can't: a public exoneration if he testifies. The beat is uneasy alliance between two people who survived by serving monsters.

chapters.title: The Auction
chapters.summary: Eze plans to destroy the painting at a private auction of deaccessioned works. Orsen and Ada infiltrate separately; Orsen creates a diversion while Ada swaps the evidence frame for a replica. They are caught leaving—Silas, unexpectedly, holds the guards at gunpoint. The beat is the plan working and immediately unraveling.

chapters.title: Eze's Version of Justice
chapters.summary: Captured and brought before Eze at his estate, Orsen hears the commander's chilling self-justification: he protected the institution by burying its sins, and Ada's survival proves the system works for those who know how to use it. The beat is the antagonist at his most persuasive—and Orsen recording every word on a live feed.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Ada's POV: with Silas's files and Orsen's live recording, they air a final emergency episode—Eze's own voice confessing, Silas's documents corroborating. Arrests begin within hours. But exposure cuts both ways: Ada's survival is now public, and the life she built is over. The beat is justice achieved at the cost of the self she constructed.

chapters.title: Aftermath, in Her Hand
chapters.summary: Ada testifies under her real name, facing Eze across a courtroom. Orsen, barred from the trial, waits outside and finally meets her mother and her properly, without ciphers. The beat is quiet reckoning—Ada realizes invisibility was never safety, only a slower kind of death, and she chooses the harder visibility.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Eze is convicted; Silas takes a reduced sentence; Grace and Ada begin the slow work of knowing each other again. Orsen ends his podcast, refusing to turn Ada's story into content, and donates the diaries to her, not the archive. The beat is release—he finally understands some truths belong to the people who lived them.

chapters.title: A New Volume
chapters.summary: Months later, Ada, restored in name and trade, begins a fresh diary—first entry, present tense, her own name. Orsen visits her studio; she shows him a painting she's restoring and, for the first time, signs her work where the world can see it. The beat is hope earned: identity reclaimed, justice imperfect but real, and two survivors no longer hiding.
